title.narrative: Output 6.3. Increased capacity of member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
The National Committee for Women’s Employment, chaired by the Minister of Labour conducted, in consultation with tripartite plus representation, a gap analysis of the relevant laws and policies in light of the Convention No. 190 and its accompanying Recommendation No. 206. The national legal and policy review was discussed and validated by the tripartite National Committee for Women’s Employment and 16 amendments were proposed for further deliberations.
Building on the recommendations of the gap analysis, the Palestinian General federation of Trade Unions formed a coalition with more than 25 members of civil society and sectoral unions with the aim to develop and carry out advocacy campaigns, as well as to embark upon policy dialogue calling for reforms of the labour law. With support from the ILO, the coalition developed its advocacy and communication plan and will begin implementing it during last quarter of 2021. The ILO has provided technical support for the gap analysis of the labour law in light of the Convention No. 190 and proposed amendments which were adopted by the tripartite National Committee for Women’s Employment. The ILO also provided technical support for the formulation of the coalition’s action plan, including amendments to laws and policies.
With a view to support the measures agreed in the action plan, the ILO, in collaboration with ITC Turin, is planning a training on C190 for tripartite constituents, for 4 weeks between 10 October and 4 November, to sensitize tripartite constituents on violence and harassment and, in particular, on gender-based violence and harassment, and its linkages with gender equality at work.
